subject: Recap & next steps — pilot savings, batching/caching levers
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@streamlinefin.com>, Priya Desai <priya@streamlinefin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps — pilot savings, batching/caching levers

Hi Amit / Priya — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap of what we heard, and the asks to get a short pilot running. TL;DR: there are clear token-cost opportunities (batching + prefix/KV caching) but we need a small trace sample and an ops window to validate latency impact.

What you told us (pain & goals)
- Primary pain: per-request token spend and month-to-month bill variability for real-time risk decissions. Current avg token bill ~$75k/mo with spikes during peak hours.
- Goal: prove a 30–50% unit-cost reduction in production-like traffic while keeping 99th pct latency within 150ms of current baseline. Pilot should be low-friction (4–6 weeks) and produce a repeatable savings playbook.

Key levers we proposed
- Batching: group short requests into micro-batches (requests with similar max-len distribution). Expected reduction: 15–30% depending on queuing tolerance.
- KV/prefix caching: cache repeated prefixes for session-based scoring (good fit for your user flows). Expected reduction: 20–35% on cacheable traffic.
- Model variant & quantization: evaluate a slightly smaller quantized variant for non-critical scoring paths (saves ~10–20% tokens+compute).
- Routing & reserved capacity: route latency-sensitive requests to Dedicated capacity and batchable/non-critical traffic to cost-optimized nodes.

Preliminary ROI framing (back-of-envelope)
- Baseline: $75k/mo token spend. If 40% combined savings, net ~$30k/mo savings. Pilot cost estimate (Redwood-hosted, 4 weeks): $6–10k — we’ll provide exact quote.

What we need from you to start the pilot
1) Sample traces (one week's anonymized request logs or 24–48h of representative traffic).
2) A short list of 3 scoring endpoints and their SLOs (p99 target, acceptable degradation).
3) A named technical point-of-contact for onboarding and an ops window for a non-prod test.
4) Confirmation on legal/compliance PO route (procurement email or DocuSign owner).

Proposed next steps
- You: share traces + endpoint list by EOD Tue (21 Apr) if possible.
- Us: we'll return a scoped pilot plan, exact pricing, and an onboarding checklist within 48 hours of receiving traces.
- Quick sync: 30-min call Thursday to review sample and finalize pilot runbook (propose Thu 22 Apr 9 AM PT).

Attachments: attached a short one-pager scope and an updated proposal (redwood-proposal-v2.pdf).

Thanks again — happy to jump on another call to walk through any of the levers.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Thanks Amit — quick answers below and we’ll include them in the formal pilot doc we send after we get traces.

Latency impact (short answer)
- Batching: for short micro-batches (<10 reqs), typical p50 change is negligible (<10ms). p99 can increase depending on queueing window; with a 30–50ms queue cap we’ve seen p99 remain within ~100–150ms of baseline.
- Cache: prefix/KV caching reduces compute and typically improves latency for cached requests (p50/p99 improve when cache hits are high).
- Routing: we propose a split: latency-critical endpoints on dedicated low-latency nodes, batchable scoring on cost-optimized instances — this preserves your p99 while letting us capture batching savings.

Trace fields (safe scrub checklist)
- timestamp, endpoint path, token_count_in, token_count_out, response_ms, request_id (hashed), feature_flags, routing_key. Do NOT include full PII fields; hashed ids are fine.

Pilot cost range
- 4-week hosted pilot estimate: $7,500 – $9,500 (depends on peak throughput and whether dedicated small pool is required). We’ll lock a firm number after trace review.

Next: we’ll take the traces, run a 48–72h simulated run to give an expected savings band and a recommended config. Meeting confirmed: Thu 22 Apr 9 AM PT works for us — I’ll send invite now.

Best,
Tessa
